about: Jaipur-based power EPC contractor that builds turnkey power distribution and transmission projects mainly for state electricity utilities (DISCOMs) across six Indian states. It has completed 36 projects worth Rs 764.67 crore and has 18 ongoing projects, with 18,579 km of distribution lines laid by July 2026. It follows an asset-light model, leasing project equipment.

promoters.background: Family-led promoter group with over 15 years in power EPC; the company was converted in 2019 from the partnership firm Swastika Electricals & Fertilizers. Four promoters sell shares in the OFS and promoters personally guarantee company borrowings.

concentration.note: Top 5 clients gave 96.87% of FY26 revenue (99.82% in FY25, 98.12% in FY24); top 10 gave 99.58%. Clients are mainly state power utilities and public sector entities.

litigation_note: No criminal or material civil cases against the company. Four tax proceedings against the company total Rs 0.45 crore; four tax proceedings against promoters total Rs 2.24 crore. Disputed claims include AVVNL price variation (about Rs 1.88 crore) and a JVVNL claim of Rs 3.60 crore.
strengths: Revenue grew from Rs 209.58 crore in FY24 to Rs 503.57 crore in FY26 (55% CAGR), and PAT grew about 72% a year.
Order book of Rs 916.55 crore (July 2026) is about 1.8 times FY26 revenue, giving visibility.
Return ratios are strong: RoNW 35.44% and ROCE 25.76% in FY26.
Asset-light model with leased equipment keeps capital spending low.
Over 15 years in power distribution EPC; 36 projects done and 18 under execution.
Many projects are World Bank or Government of India funded, which supports payment reliability.
Debt to equity improved to 0.73 in FY26 from 1.44 in FY25.
Priced at 11.78 times FY26 EPS at the cap price, within the listed peer P/E range of 10.1 to 14.6.

risks.title: Extreme client concentration
risks.detail: Top 5 clients, mainly state power utilities, gave 96.87% of FY26 revenue and top 10 gave 99.58%. Losing or delayed payment from one DISCOM would hit results hard.

risks.title: Negative operating cash flow every year
risks.detail: Operating cash flow was -Rs 3.34 crore (FY24), -Rs 76.54 crore (FY25) and -Rs 9.65 crore (FY26) despite rising profits, as receivables and retention money build up.

risks.title: Working-capital heavy and debt funded
risks.detail: Borrowings are Rs 114.64 crore, almost all short-term; trade receivables are Rs 114.98 crore and retention money Rs 160.02 crore. Some facilities are repayable on demand and secured on assets.

risks.title: Large contingent liabilities
risks.detail: Bank guarantees of Rs 272.68 crore at March 2026 are about 7 times PAT and 164 times cash. Invocation would strain finances.

risks.title: Related-party dealings
risks.detail: Purchases from a promoter-linked firm (MG Engineering) were Rs 11.86 crore in FY26. Loans of Rs 12.65 crore were taken from and repaid to Parnami Incense, and promoters draw salaries and rent.

risks.title: Order book execution and delays
risks.detail: The company has had delays in most projects in the last three years. Order book of Rs 916.55 crore may not convert fully to revenue.

risks.title: Promoter guarantees, control and OFS
risks.detail: Promoters personally guarantee borrowings and keep 57.41% after the issue. The OFS of Rs 32.38 crore goes to selling shareholders, not the company.

risks.title: Subcontractor reliance and compliance lapses
risks.detail: Subcontractor cost was Rs 98.47 crore (21.87% of FY26 expenses), up from 11.70% in FY25. There were delays in GST and ESIC payments, including a Rs 11.87 crore GSTR-3B filing delay in FY26.

notes: Standalone restated FY24-FY26 figures; source tables in lakhs converted to Rs crore. Balance sheet and cash flow tables were garbled in extraction and were reconciled using totals and the reported debt/equity and RoNW. Borrowings = current + non-current; cash_and_bank = cash and equivalents + other bank balances; reserves = other equity; EBITDA per company KPI table. NAV 57.69 is FY26; ROE not reported. A pre-IPO placement of 24,24,242 shares at Rs 165 (Rs 40 crore) reduced the fresh issue. Order book shown is as of July 31, 2026 (Rs 916.55 crore); FY26 year-end order book was Rs 687.44 crore. Reservation percentages computed from share counts. founded_year is the 2019 conversion of a partnership firm. govt_share_pct left null as no percentage is stated.
